item.content:encoded:
1) So that when a large flock is created for observation, the object can safely be moved out of the test room. It's a hell of a lot easier than trying to herd the whole flock out of the way.

2) No. They're too small to be generally perceived as separate entities, which is part of the definition of an Eligible Group: five or more items that a casual observer can't tell apart except by color.

3) Nope, no living things.

4) The number of batteries in 243 is related to a lot of things, including power, range, selection criteria, and stability. The Foundation isn't likely to find that out, though, because whenever a battery is added, it and all the others in 243 flock up for 24 hours or so. They'll eventually settle back down into the fused aggregate we're familiar with, but the Foundation does not like what happens in the meantime. Turns out that whatever usually holds the batteries together can really screw around with concepts like movement and emoting.

Intern VS Employee
It is stated above that the implied link between 1507 and 243 is via Pixar animation. This implies that their success would have been due at least in part to the use of of 243 which begs the question of why hasn't Pixar gone under or suffered significant loss of quality after its removal? If the SCP's were brought in by an intern and not a full time employee it would potentially explain this lack of decline in quality.

MC&D VS Anartist
The fact that that 243 was used to create art seems to imply that the creator was an Anartist or at least that 243 was created by an anartist. While there is certainly no standing expectation or rule that says something like 243 couldn't have just appeared out of thin air or by its own accord and have been found and used by Pixar ultimately it ended up in Pixar's hand meaning
1. They obtained it second or third hand having already been existing on its own/created by someone else or
2. They obtained it first hand by it coming into existence by its own accord or though the either direct or indirect actions of Pixar that caused it to come into existence.
MC&D are pretty much the only major distributor of these kinds of things so it would seem obvious to implicate them.

I have some rough drafts of Emails on the sandbox as well as a AWCY variant; though the more I think about it the more it seems less fitting to use AWCY's as its not their MO in the least bit, but ultimately it seems pointless to work on either of those if the basic idea is rejected in the first place, hence my posting it.

I'd say its far more likely that the object that animates inanimate objects and makes them display flocking behaviors (just like 1507 does in fact demonstrate) animated 1507 and something unique happened with the effect to make it last longer. 1507 has no ability to impart animation onto other objects, and since that is the main effect of 243, saying 243 is a failed copy of 1507 just doesn't really work.

Addendum 2: Given the release of █████ Animation Studios's film "Knick Knack" prior to containment of SCP-243, in which a flamingo is a one of several characters, it is currently hypothesized that SCP-243 may be a possible origin for SCP-1507. The style movement observed in SCP-1507 instances matches movement observed from the character in the film, and the effects of SCP-243 would explain the former's flocking behaviors. If SCP-243 is the origin of SCP-1507, it is currently unknown why SCP-1507 has yet to deanimate, or if it will deanimate in accordance to SCP-243's behavior in the future.

Something along these lines?

Very belatedly, sorry! This definitely does affect both clothing and guns. Weaponry with mass-produced ammunition is strictly forbidden around it. Uniforms are… well, not usually dangerous (though I'd think twice about matching neckties), but inconvenient. An animated shirt would probably desert you to join the flock; it might then, later, come back and try to put itself on you with or without your cooperation, or it might start waltzing with a nearby flock of clothes hangers. It's unpredictable.

Suffice to say that personnel working with this thing are strongly encouraged to wear plainclothes.
